Repo: Tendril (current directory). Contest: timed intervals. Main files are likely shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/tendril/app/data/track/TimeLog.kt, TimeLogDao.kt, domain/track/TimeTracker.kt, TimeLogTotals.kt, domain/plan/DayTotals.kt, domain/review/, and the sync mappers (sync/SnapshotMappers.kt, SnapshotRecords.kt).
Claims from the map:
1. TimeLog stores startedAt, endedAt and either an entryId or a habitId. List every column with its type and nullability.
Claims about behaviour (verify each; quote the rule):
2. A running timer is a TimeLog with endedAt null; say how many may run at once and what starting a second one does.
3. A TimeLog may reference neither an entry nor a habit (a free-standing interval); say whether it carries its own label or note.
4. Deleting the entry or habit deletes, orphans or keeps its time logs (foreign key or code).
5. Where totals are computed (per entry, per day, per review) and whether overlapping intervals are counted twice.
6. Manual entry or editing of a past interval exists.
7. How TimeLog rows sync (tombstoned, delete-wins, last-writer-wins).

Repo: Chronicle (current directory). Contest: timed intervals. Main files are likely data/src/main/kotlin/com/hazia/chronicle/data/room/entity/SessionEntity.kt, ActivityEntity.kt, CategoryEntity.kt, core/data/.../track/ActivityRepository.kt, the Room DAO (dao/CoreDao.kt), EntityMappers.kt, and the backup/FolderSync code.
Claims from the map:
1. SessionEntity stores activity sessions (a start and an end). List every column with its type and nullability, and every ActivityEntity column.
Claims about behaviour (verify each; quote the rule):
2. A running session has no end; say how many may run at once and what starting a second one does.
3. A session must belong to an Activity; say whether an Activity links to a tracker, a category or anything else.
4. Deleting an Activity deletes, orphans or keeps its sessions.
5. Where totals or charts over sessions are computed, and whether overlapping sessions are counted twice.
6. Manual entry or editing of a past session exists; a session can carry a note.
7. How SessionEntity rows sync (per-field stamps, tombstones, 90-day GC).
